propositions: Prose guides cite criterion ids inline without coupling to the registry, allowing criterion rubric rewrites to silently contradict guide claims for months.

A pin manifest approach forces re-verification by digesting each cited criterion's authoritative text and failing the gate when the digest changes, surfacing the divergence as a gate failure rather than silent drift.

Citation extraction matches only the registry's closed criterion-id vocabulary at word boundaries against guide prose, independent of markup or structure, so ordinary prose edits and restructures do not break the gate.

The gate integrates into the existing validate-routing composition without a new CI step, and comprises a new module (guide_parity.py), a generated manifest (criterion-pins.json), and tests that verify stale pins, unknown citations, orphans, and idempotence.
Mutating a cited criterion's registry text must cause the gate to report a stale pin naming both the criterion and the citing guide, making the 828a class of silent semantic drift detectable in CI.
